practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: No @Tag/@Category or equivalent annotations are present on the class or method, so tests cannot be easily categorized for selective execution.

The test performs two distinct 'Act' operations: heap.min() (inspection) and heap.retiraMin() (mutation expecting exception). This counts as multiple behaviors in one test rather than a single Arrange-Act-Assert block.
Test uses only local variables and does not rely on shared mutable state or execution order. No @Before/@After are required given local-only state.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: The class contains only this single test that covers an empty-heap (error) scenario but no happy-path (e.g., successful insertion and retrieval) tests for the same functionality; the class lacks complementary normal-flow tests.
The test checks behavior on an empty heap (a boundary condition). This is an explicit edge-case check (empty collection).

The test is short, self-contained, uses no duplicated logic across multiple tests (only one test present) and follows Arrange-Act-Assert structure; no helpers are necessary for this single, small test.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test is small (well under 20-30 lines), linear, with no loops or complex conditionals, so cyclomatic complexity is low.
The test contains multiple meaningful assertions (assertNull and an exception content check), verifying different aspects of behavior rather than a single superficial assertion.
There are no @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test methods; the test is active and runnable (has timeout but active).
The class Javadoc explicitly lists requirement traceability (REQ-HEAP-001, REQ-HEAP-002, REQ-HEAP-003), linking tests to requirements.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses an explicit timeout (@Test(timeout = 4000)), which is an explicit timing-based assertion; per decision rules this counts as an explicit performance-related constraint and is compliant.
The method name 'test9' is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome; it fails the recommended descriptive naming convention.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: There are signs of automated test generation: import of EvoSuite runtime classes and a generic test name 'test9' consistent with generated tests. This indicates likely heavy code generation patterns.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The class-level comment explicitly states Given-When-Then and the test contains clear scenario comments; this shows evidence of design intent and BDD-style structure.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with the public FPHeapMin API (min and retiraMin) and does not use reflection or verify private internals, thus focusing on observable behavior.

Assertions are specific and include a descriptive failure message for assertNull; the exception content is also checked via assertExceptionContains rather than a generic assertTrue, meeting the recommendation.
Comments use Given-When-Then which explain intent rather than trivial step-by-step comments; there is no commented-out code or excessive commentary.
The test uses no sources of non-determinism (no Random, no current time, no Thread.sleep) and uses only local state, so results should be deterministic.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses only local variables, does not persist data or modify static/shared state, and therefore avoids side effects.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: There are no categorization annotations (@Tag, @Category) on the test class or method; per decision rules this absence means tests are not categorized for selective execution.
The test contains a single Act operation (heap.retiraMin()) and a single Arrange-Act-Assert flow (construct heap, call retiraMin, expect exception). No multiple unrelated operations are present.
The test uses only local variables (no shared static/instance state) and there are no @Before/@After setup dependencies visible; thus it is independent of other tests.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: The class contains a single test method that covers an exceptional flow only. There is no visible happy-path test for the same behavior or class; decision rule: class has < 2 test methods so mark non-compliant.
Test uses a single typical capacity value (159) and does not exercise boundary values (0, negative, max). No explicit boundary tests or names present.
The test is short and self-contained (< 10 lines) with no duplicated code or need for helper methods; no repeated blocks to refactor within the shown class.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: The test is small (< 20 lines) and contains no loops or nested conditionals; complexity is low and follows a linear flow with a try/catch for expected exception handling.

The test contains effectively one substantive assertion (assertExceptionContains). It does not verify multiple properties of the result/exception (e.g., type, message, other state), so assertions are relatively superficial.
No @Ignore/@Disabled annotations or commented-out @Test lines are present; the test is active and runnable (has @Test).
Class-level Javadoc includes explicit requirement traceability (REQ-HEAP-001, REQ-HEAP-002, REQ-HEAP-003), satisfying traceability criteria.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses an explicit timeout parameter (@Test(timeout = 4000)), which counts as an explicit performance-related assertion per decision rules, so this practice is marked compliant.
The method name 'test5' is generic and does not follow descriptive naming patterns (e.g., method_scenario_expected). Decision rule: generic test name marks non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: No explicit auto-generated markers or verbose generated comments are present in the class. Although the method name looks generated, there is no clear evidence of heavy code generation, so mark as not-applicable.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: The test uses Given/When/Then inline comments, showing BDD-style intent and evidence of thoughtful design per the decision rules.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test exercises public API (constructor and retiraMin) without reflection or access to private internals; no evidence of brittle coupling to implementation details.

The test uses specific assertion helper assertExceptionContains and includes a fail(...) message. At least one assertion includes a descriptive message (the fail), meeting the >=50% messages rule for this single method's assertions.
The method contains minimal, purposeful comments (Given, When/Then) and the class has useful Javadoc; there is no commented-out code or excessive commentary.
No sources of non-determinism (no Random, no System.currentTimeMillis(), no Thread.sleep()) and test uses only local state, so results should be deterministic.
